name: Sallu
overview: Sallu was a male priest from the tribe of Levi, explicitly identified as a descendant of Aaron. He is noted for being among the priests who returned with Zerubbabel during the post-exilic period, as recorded in Nehemiah 12:7. His role as a priest highlights his participation in the restoration of temple worship after the Babylonian exile.
namesAndTitles: The name Sallu appears only once in Scripture and is a proper name that possibly means "he restores." This meaning aligns well with his role in the restoration period, though the name itself is not indicated to be divinely given.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Sallu was a descendant of Aaron, the first high priest, establishing his priestly lineage. No other family relationships are documented beyond this connection.
scriptureSignificance: Sallu's significance lies in his priestly service during the crucial time of Israel's return from exile and the rebuilding of the temple. Being among the priests who accompanied Zerubbabel underscores his involvement in reestablishing proper worship according to the Law. His Aaronic descent affirms the continuity of the priestly line through a period of great national restoration.
